role.admin: Admin: everything except managing the owner
setup.title: First run
setup.lead: Create the owner account: it has full access to Gridlume.
setup.code.hint: For example K7QM-2R9X. Case and dash do not matter.
setup.password.hint: At least 10 characters. Keep it in a password manager.
login.title: Sign in to Gridlume
err.internal: Something went wrong in the core. Details are in its log.
err.offline: No connection to the core. Check that it is running.
err.bad_json: The core did not understand the request. Reload the page.
err.csrf: The request was blocked by protection. Reload the page.
err.forbidden: Not allowed: you have read-only access.
err.unauthorized: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
err.not_found: This no longer exists: it may have been deleted in another tab.
err.already_set_up: The owner already exists. Sign in.
err.too_many_attempts: Too many attempts. Wait a minute.
err.code.invalid: The code is wrong. Check it in the core's console.
err.username.invalid: Username: up to 40 characters, no spaces or slashes.
err.password.too_short: The password is too short: at least 10 characters.
err.parentId.too_deep: Nesting is one level only: a machine and what runs on it.
err.parentId.cycle: A node cannot be inside itself.
err.toId.cycle: A link must join two different nodes.
err.speedMbit.invalid: Speed is a whole number of megabits per second.
err.v.not_found: The chosen item was not found: reload the page.
map.empty.title: The map is empty
map.empty.lead: Start with areas (home, country house, cloud, a project — anything), then add machines and join them with links. Drag from a node's edge to draw a link.
map.portal.tip: Outside this machine. Double-click to go back
add.place.tip: An area is a coloured backdrop with a name that groups nodes: a flat, a country house, a cloud, a project, a team — anything.
add.node.tip: A machine, router, cloud server, domain, service or device
add.link.tip: What is connected to what, and why. Faster: drag from a node's edge.
f.name: Name
f.subtitle: Caption
f.subtitle.hint: Short line under the name, e.g. "Debian 13 · AV1 encoding"
f.inside.hint: For containers and services: the machine they run on
f.state.hint: Until an agent reports it, the state is set by hand. "Planned" means it does not exist yet.
f.about.hint: Shown in the map tooltip. Write it for yourself six months from now.
link.uplink.hint: Where "To" gets the internet from. If it fails, "To" and everything behind it go offline.
link.lan.hint: A physical LAN connection: "From" provides the network, "To" receives it.
link.wifi.hint: A wireless connection: "From" is the access point, "To" is the client.
link.vpn.hint: An encrypted tunnel between sites. Direction does not matter.
link.runs.hint: "From" runs on "To". The arrow points at the host.
link.depends.hint: "From" cannot work without "To". The arrow points at what it needs.
link.db.hint: "From" keeps its data in the "To" database.
link.queue.hint: "From" writes or reads messages in the "To" queue.
link.dns.hint: The "From" domain points at the "To" address.
about.vpn: Tunnel between {from} and {to}: reach machines on the other side.
broken.uplink: {to} and everything behind it lose the internet.
broken.vpn: Machines on the other side become unreachable remotely.
broken.dns: The site stops opening by name.
insp.notes.help: Anything for yourself: how it is set up, where the config is, what to check when it fails. Saved when you leave the field.
insp.notes.ph: How it is set up, where the config is, what to do on failure…
insp.links.none: No links yet. Drag from this node's edge to another one.
insp.breaks.help: Worked out from "runs on", "depends on", network and power links. Planned links are ignored.
insp.breaks.none: Nothing: no node depends on this one.
insp.needs.help: The whole chain, e.g. service → machine → router → internet.
insp.what.none: Not described. Press "Edit" to explain it.
insp.swap.tip: Swap "from" and "to". Changes the dependency calculation.
insp.place.help: Top-level nodes inside this area. Drag a node into the area to make it part of it.
insp.place.empty: Empty. Drag a node here or add a new one.
del.title: Delete "{name}"
del.node.nothing: The node has no links; deleting it affects nothing else.
del.node.kids: {count, plural, one {# node inside is deleted with it.} other {# nodes inside are deleted with it.}}
del.node.links: {count, plural, one {# link is deleted.} other {# links are deleted.}}
del.node.breaks: {count, plural, one {# node on the map depends on it.} other {# nodes on the map depend on it.}}
del.link: The link disappears from the map and from the dependency calculation. The nodes stay.
del.place: {count, plural, =0 {The area disappears. It has no nodes.} other {The area disappears; # nodes stay on the map outside areas.}}
add.agent.tip: One command on the machine and it appears on the map by itself, with live numbers: CPU, memory, disks, network.
agent.title: Agent
agent.connect.tip: Install the agent on this machine: its state and load become live.
agent.lead: The agent is a small program on the machine. It connects to Gridlume by itself, so no ports need to be opened on the machine. First choose how much it may do.
agent.mode.user.sees: Runs as the user gridlume in the docker group. Sees the machine and containers; does not see disk SMART or other users' processes.
agent.mode.user.risk: If the agent is compromised: through Docker, effectively the whole machine; but the process itself is not root and the service is restricted.
agent.mode.readonly.sees: Own user without write access to Docker. Sees machine metrics; cannot manage containers.
agent.mode.readonly.risk: If the agent is compromised: almost nothing, only look. Suits companies.
agent.mode.root.sees: Runs as root. Sees everything without setup.
agent.mode.root.risk: If the agent is compromised: the whole machine. Simple, but not safe.
agent.core.hint: The machine must be able to open this address. If Gridlume is behind a VPN, use the VPN address.
agent.core.local: This address only works on this computer. Enter one the machine can reach, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:7420.
agent.waiting: Waiting for the agent to connect…
agent.unlink.tip: The agent stops sending data. The node, its links and history stay.
agent.unlink.title: Unlink the agent from "{name}"
agent.unlink.what: The agent on the machine can no longer connect. The node, links and history stay. To remove it from the machine: sudo systemctl disable --now gridlume-agent.
live.now.help: Updates every 5 seconds. A bar turns amber from 80% and red from 95%.
live.cpu: CPU · {cores, plural, one {# core} other {# cores}}, {threads, plural, one {# thread} other {# threads}}
live.load.tip: How many tasks wait for the CPU (1-minute average). Above {n} (the number of threads) the machine cannot keep up.
live.history.help: The line is the average, the light area the maximum per interval. Kept for 14 days.
live.history.empty: History is building up: the first points appear in a couple of minutes.
err.nodeId.not_machine: An agent goes only on a top-level machine: server, VM, cloud server.
docker.title: Docker
docker.title.help: Containers of this machine appear inside it by themselves. Open the machine to see them and the links between them.
docker.total: of {count, plural, one {# container} other {# containers}}
docker.error.no_access: The agent may not read Docker. In "Own user" mode it must be in the docker group; in "Read only" mode the gridlume-docker-ro proxy must be running.
docker.error.unavailable: Docker is installed but does not answer. Check: systemctl status docker.
docker.container.help: Data comes from the machine's agent every 5 seconds. Environment values (passwords, tokens) never leave the machine.
docker.gone.long: The machine no longer has this container. If it was removed for good, delete the node too; if it is re-created with the same name, the node comes back to life.
docker.ports.tip: Left: the port on the machine; right: inside the container. Without an arrow the port is only inside the Docker network.
docker.restarts.tip: How many times Docker restarted the container after it crashed. If it grows, the container keeps crashing.
docker.name: Name and id
suggest.title: {count, plural, one {Looks like # link} other {Looks like # links}}
suggest.lead: Found in the Docker settings. Confirm and the link appears on the map with an explanation.
suggest.env: The variables of {from} name the address "{host}".
setup.fromLink: The code from the link is filled in: choose a username and password.
setup.noLink: Open the link the installer showed at the end. If it is lost, run this on the Gridlume machine:
settings.title: Settings
update.title: Updates
update.button.tip: First a database copy, then the swap and a start check. If the new version does not come up, the old one and its database come back. The panel is away for about half a minute.
update.running: Updating to {to}… This page refreshes by itself.
update.upToDate: This is the latest version of the channel.
update.manualOnly: The core was not started by the installer, so it cannot update from the panel: this page only tells about new versions.
update.last.rolled_back: Version {to} did not start; {from} is back
update.channel.stable.tip: Released versions only, e.g. 0.2.0. Less often, but checked as a whole.
update.channel.edge.tip: A build after every change, e.g. 0.3.0-dev.12 — a preview of the next release. New things at once, rough edges possible.
update.auto.hint: Checked every 6 hours. With a database copy and rollback, like a manual update.
update.badge.tip: A new Gridlume version is available. Open update settings.
core.here.tip: The Gridlume core runs on this machine. If it stops, the panel goes too.
err.not_installed: The core was not started by the installer: update it by hand.
account.title: Account
account.password.lead: You stay signed in here; every other device is signed out.
account.changed: Password changed. Other sessions are signed out.
err.password.same: The new password is the same as the current one.
pref.minimap.hint: A small copy of the map in the bottom right: areas in their colour, nodes in the colour of their state. Resize it by its top-left corner.
pref.linkLabels.hint: Protocol and speed on every line. Off: only on the selected link.
pref.device: These are kept in this browser: another device can have its own.
map.path: Where you are on the map
map.path.place: Show this area on the map
menu.label: Actions
overview.label: Minimap: click a node to go there, drag to move the view
overview.resize: Drag to resize. Double-click for the usual size.
map.handle.tip: Drag to another node to link them, or to empty space to create a new linked node
update.problem.signature: release signature does not match: not installable
update.ahead: The installed build is newer than the latest in the "{channel}" channel ({v}). An update comes when that channel has something newer. Going back to an older version is not offered: its database may not understand the newer data.
update.otherNewer: The "{channel}" channel has {v}, newer than installed. Choose that channel to get it.
update.stuck: The update request has waited over two minutes: the update service on the machine seems to be off. Check:
update.last.interrupted: The update to {to} was interrupted (the machine restarted or the service stopped)
update.reloaded.title: Gridlume was updated to {v}
update.reloaded.lead: The page will reload by itself once you finish with the open window or field.
insp.resize: Drag left to make the panel wider (up to 640 px). Double-click for the usual width.
rail.label: Sections
agent.update.tip: The agent downloads the new build from this core, checks its signature and restarts. If the new version does not connect, the old one comes back.
agent.update.error: Could not ask the agent to update: it went offline or is already up to date.
agent.update.noUpdater: Version {v} is available, but this agent was installed before updates from Gridlume existed. Run this on the machine once:
agent.update.rolled_back: Version {to} did not connect; {from} is back
update.agentAuto.hint: When the core has a newer agent build, agents install it themselves, with a signature check and rollback. A version that once failed to connect is only retried with the button.
